summary: Catalog's 13 path-id transition writes have no organizer at any layer
description:
**Surfaced by TKT-245's ai-review [high], and confirmed by execution.** The agreed
second slice of TKT-245, which closed the 15 body-organizer writes and the channel read.

Thirteen unsafe catalog operations take only a **path id** and reach the store with **no organizer at
any layer**:

```
POST /series/{id}/publish            POST /festivals/{id}/publish
POST /series/{id}/archive            POST /festivals/{id}/archive
POST /series/{id}/performances       POST /festivals/{id}/days
POST /performances/{id}/publish      POST /seasons/{id}/series
POST /performances/{id}/archive      POST /seasons/{id}/events
POST /performances/{id}/close        POST /seat-maps/{id}/publish
POST /performances/{id}/reopen
```

`store.PublishSeries(ctx, id uuid.UUID)` — the organizer appears in neither the handler nor the
store signature. There is no asserted field to distrust because there is no field at all, which is
why TKT-245's remedy (an assertion replacing a body field) does not reach them.

**The attach operations are the sharpest case**, verified at the store tier:
`AttachPerformanceToSeries` (`services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go:184-202`) reads
`organizer_id` from **both** rows and compares them **to each other** — never to a caller. Two
resources belonging to the same victim tenant satisfy it. A caller holding
`CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` can therefore publish, archive, close, reopen or re-wire another
organizer's resources by id, and public catalog responses expose those ids.

**Conditions of Success:**
- Every one of the 13 takes the organizer from the **verified assertion scope** and passes it into
  the store, inside the same locked lookup/update predicate — not a check before it.
- `TestEveryHandlerReadingTheVerifiedOrganizerRequiresTheAssertion` (added in TKT-245) covers them
  automatically once their handlers call `organizerFor`; the invariant already asserts both
  directions, so no new test infrastructure is needed for coverage — but each transition needs a
  cross-tenant refusal test **at the store tier**, because a fake store scopes in Go and would pass
  with the SQL predicate deleted (AGENTS.md, TKT-236).
- **ADR-058 § what this does NOT close item 5 must be amended**, not deleted: it currently states
  the boundary is false for the transitions, and that sentence becomes wrong the day this lands.

Quality gates: `make check`; `make browser` if any back-office form changes.

Non-goals: the assertion mechanism itself (shipped, ADR-058); roles (catalog enforces none).

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Filed from TKT-245's ai-review — confirmed, deliberately deferred

ai-review raised this as **[high] "Path-ID writes still permit cross-tenant mutation"**. Every word
of the finding is correct and I verified it at the store tier rather than taking it on trust.

**Why it was overridden rather than fixed in TKT-245:** it is the agreed slice boundary — the owner
chose the 15/13 split at Gate 1 after both classes were enumerated — and the remedy is genuinely
different. TKT-245 replaced a body field with a credential; this needs a **store-tier organizer
predicate** on lookup, which is a different change in a different layer, and folding it into a
43-file diff would have meant a second implementation reviewed by nobody.

The residual is named in three places so it cannot be lost: ADR-058 §5, the PR description, and
here. **The reviewer's own sentence conceded the point** — *"ADR-058 acknowledges 13 such operations,
but that means the claimed tenant boundary is incomplete"* — and it is incomplete, which the ADR says
before anyone asks.

Needs shaping before Gate 1. The likely trap: the attach operations already compare two organizers to
each other, so a fix that merely *adds* a caller comparison beside that check would look correct and
leave the lookup unscoped — the predicate has to be in the SQL, under the same lock.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Shaping pass - readiness verdict: **PASS** (8/8 met, 0 open, 0 deferred)

Shaped from a **Backlog** start. The run was requested as "autonomous", and Gate 1 stays human in
autonomous mode, so this stops here for prioritization rather than self-promoting to Ready.

Every claim in the ticket text was **verified against the code** rather than inherited (shaping.md
s"a remedy proposed in the ticket text is a hypothesis"). All of them held - which is itself worth
recording, because the checking is what makes that trustworthy.

| DoR item | State | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| objective | met | Confirmed at the store tier |
| scope | met | 13 in, residuals + roles out |
| uncertainties | met | 3 resolved by reading, 0 remaining |
| dependencies | met | Zero open blockers; TKT-245 merged |
| approach | met | Verified; see the four findings below |
| first_slice | met | One slice, all 13 (splitting breaks an invariant) |
| success | met | COS verified achievable as written |
| context_memo | met | Baked: 7 governingAdrs, 6 governingTests, all resolve at HEAD |

#### What the read changed vs. what the ticket assumed

**1. The trap the filing comment predicted is real, and confirmed.** `AttachPerformanceToSeries`
(`store/postgres.go:184-202`) reads `organizer_id` from both rows and compares them **to each
other** (`targetOrg != orgID`), never to a caller. Two resources of the same victim tenant satisfy
it. A fix that merely *adds* a caller comparison beside that check would look correct and leave the
lookup unscoped.

**2. Where the predicate goes, precisely.** `transitionSeries` does
`SELECT id FROM series WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE` (`postgres.go:1070`). That statement gains
`AND organizer_id=$2`. ADR-018 is why it must be *inside* the locked lookup rather than beside it:
a check outside the lock is a TOCTOU on the row the transition is about to move.

**3. The slice is smaller than "13" suggests, in two independent ways.**
- **Store:** the transitions share helpers - `transitionSeries` and `transitionFestival` each back
  2 operations, `attachSeasonMember` backs 2 - so 13 operations collapse to **~9 store edit points**.
- **Front end:** 11 of the 13 appear in `web/` **only in `api-types.gen.ts`**. They have no
  hand-written caller at all. Only `publishSeatMap` and `publishPerformance` are actually invoked.

**4. The back-office change is threading an existing value, not new plumbing.** `postCatalog`
already takes an `assertion` argument, and `staff.organizerAssertion` is already in scope in the
very handler that calls `publishSeatMap(mapId)` without it (`venues/[id].astro:89`) - three lines
above, a sibling write passes it. Same shape in `events/new.astro:142`.

#### Confirmed, so the plan need not re-derive it

- **All 13 are genuinely undeclared.** They inherit the **document-level** default
  (`security: [CatalogStaffWriteCredential]`, `openapi.yaml:21-22`); none has an operation-level
  block. First measured with a regex that bled into the *next* operation and reported 3 of 13 as
  already converted - corrected by parsing per-operation. Recorded because the wrong number was
  briefly convincing.
- **The COS claim about auto-coverage is correct.**
  `TestEveryHandlerReadingTheVerifiedOrganizerRequiresTheAssertion` derives its set from the **Go
  AST**, so the 13 enter coverage the moment their handlers call `organizerFor`, and Direction 2
  forces the contract declaration to follow. No new API-tier infrastructure.
- **A directly reusable store-tier template exists**:
  `TestUpdateChannelIsScopedToTheOwningOrganizer`, including the `ErrNotFound`-not-mismatch subtlety
  (a distinguishing refusal confirms a guessed id is real) and the both-directions structure
  ("a boundary, not a wall"). Note `//go:build smoke`.

#### Flagged for the plan (not blocking Gate 1)

- **`make browser` is required.** `publishSeatMap` and `publishPerformance` are reached from Astro
  form POST handlers, so this touches back-office write paths (AGENTS.md). Note the sharp edge: **no
  form markup changes** here, so a render-only spec would prove nothing - and a browser spec cannot
  see the SSR handler's upstream call. Assert what the browser can see or what the write left behind.
- **`publishSeatMap` is ADR-029 territory.** Seat-map edits are family-scoped under
  `pg_advisory_xact_lock(map_family_id)`, *not* a row lock on the current version. Re-resolve the
  current version after taking the lock.
- **`risk:low` must NOT be claimed.** This is an auth/trust-boundary change across ~24 files. Stated
  explicitly so the claim comment inherits a verdict rather than a silence.

**Verdict: PASS.** No open items, no `deferred`, no blockers, no human decisions outstanding. The
ticket is claimable the moment it is prioritized.

**Waiting on Gate 1** - the human transitions Backlog -> Ready. (`approach` is `met`, not
`deferred`, which matters here: shaping.md forbids `approach: deferred` on auth surfaces precisely
because the approach *is* the redesign.)

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->

**Gate 1 was the human's and was taken by the human.** The owner prioritized TKT-251 in-session and

**Branch:** `TKT-251-transition-organizer-predicate` off `origin/main` @ `3b2e882a`.

#### Risk verdict - `risk:low` is NOT claimed

Stated explicitly rather than by silence, because the label's carve-outs are exactly the tickets
whose risk is obvious to the claimer and invisible in the thread afterwards. This ticket hits **two**
carve-outs directly: it is an **auth / trust-boundary** change (it decides which tenant may mutate a

#### Mémo revalidation at claim time - diffed, not re-read

Per `decomposition.md`: checking whether the listed ADRs still hold catches supersession but cannot
catch an ADR that landed after `capturedAt` and was never listed - the more dangerous case, because
the mémo reads complete.

Listed `docs/adr/` by commit date against `capturedAt: 2026-08-16`: **nothing landed after the
bake.** The newest registry change is TKT-245's ADR-058 (2026-08-16), which is already the mémo's
primary binding and this ticket's governing decision. No supersessions, no unlisted arrivals. The
7 `governingAdrs` and 6 `governingTests` stand as baked.

#### Entering Planning

`config.models.plan` is `gpt-5.6-luna` (delegated draft, read-only), critiqued by `main-agent` -
cross-model invariant satisfied in both pairs (`plan` != `planReview`, `implement` != `aiReview`).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft - by `gpt-5.6-luna` (config.models.plan), read-only

Delegated per `config.models.plan`. Ran against the intended scope (it read the contract, the
handlers, the store, the back office and the existing tests), returned a conclusive plan, and
modified nothing - `git status` clean, verified. **Two of my brief's own facts were refuted by the
drafter**, which is the outcome the brief explicitly invited; both refutations checked and accepted
(see the critique).

One shaping discrepancy: `TestStaffCredentialAloneCanNoLongerEnumerateOrMutateAcrossTenants` exists in `services/catalog/internal/api/channels_test.go`, not `write_credential_test.go`, and currently covers channels only. Also, current `PublishSeatMap` uses a conditional `UPDATE` and does not take the family advisory lock described in the ticket; the plan treats that as work to resolve, not as already satisfied.

## 1. DoD

- All 13 OpenAPI operations require one security object containing both:
  - `CatalogStaffWriteCredential`
  - `CatalogOrganizerAssertion`
- All 13 handlers call `organizerFor` and pass the verified organizer to the store.
- Store methods accept organizer scope and enforce `(id, organizer_id)` in the locked lookup or update predicate.
- Cross-organizer attempts return `ErrNotFound`, do not mutate the victim, and do not produce a distinguishing mismatch error.
- The attach operations scope both rows independently; the existing same-organizer comparison is not used as authorization.
- Series/festival grouped-member behavior remains unchanged: members cannot publish/archive themselves.
- Seat-map publishing follows the family advisory-lock/re-resolve-current-version rule from ADR-029.
- Store-tier smoke tests cover all 13 operations against real PostgreSQL.
- ADR-058 item 5 remains present but is amended to state that the staff-token-holder transition gap is closed by TKT-251.
- Generated code is regenerated and committed before `make check`.
- No browser test is added: no form markup changes in this ticket.

## 2. Files

### Contract and generated output

- [`services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:21)
  - Add operation-level security requirements to the 13 operations:
    `publishSeatMap`, `publishPerformance`, `archivePerformance`, `closeSlot`,
    `reopenSlot`, `attachPerformanceToSeries`, `publishSeries`, `archiveSeries`,
    `attachSeriesToSeason`, `attachEventToSeason`, `attachDayToFestival`,
    `publishFestival`, and `archiveFestival`.
  - Use one requirement object, never two alternatives.
  - Keep the existing document-level staff credential and existing 401 responses.

- [`services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go)
  - Regenerate from the OpenAPI source. The generated middleware must install the organizer assertion security context for the 13 newly protected operations.

- [`web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts) and [`web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts)
  - Regenerate with `make generate`.
  - Security metadata may produce no TypeScript diff, but the generated outputs must be checked and committed if changed.

### API handlers and test doubles

- [`services/catalog/internal/api/server.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:747)
  - Update all 13 handlers to call `organizerFor`.
  - Pass the returned organizer to the store methods.
  - Preserve existing body validation and event-emission behavior.
  - In particular, ensure `PublishPerformance` no longer has an unscoped fallback read after a failed scoped update.

- [`services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go:163)
  - Update `fakeStore` method signatures.
  - Add a spy/wiring assertion that each converted handler passes the organizer from the verified assertion, not `uuid.Nil` or another value.
  - Keep fake-store tests supplementary; they do not replace PostgreSQL predicate tests.

- [`services/catalog/internal/api/channels_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/channels_test.go:815)
  - Correct or extend the existing residual-boundary test if it is made to cover path-id transitions.
  - Do not delete it. Its current location differs from the ticket brief.

### Store interface and implementation

- [`services/catalog/internal/store/store.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/store.go:509)
  - Add `organizerID uuid.UUID` to all 13 affected store signatures.
  - Document that an `(id, organizerID)` miss is `ErrNotFound`.

- [`services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go)
  - `AttachPerformanceToSeries`: scope both the series and performance locked lookups by organizer; retain the event equality check.
  - `AttachDayToFestival`: scope both festival and performance locked lookups by organizer; retain kind/status/group checks.
  - `attachSeasonMember`: scope both season and member lookups by organizer; retain membership conflict behavior.
  - `transitionSeries`: add organizer to the locked series lookup used by both publish/archive.
  - `transitionFestival`: add organizer to the locked festival lookup used by both publish/archive.
  - `PublishPerformance`: make the organizer part of the atomic update predicate and ensure the idempotent/error fallback is also organizer-scoped.
  - `ArchivePerformance`: add organizer to the `FOR UPDATE` lookup.
  - `toggleClosure`: add organizer to the `FOR UPDATE` lookup, covering both close and reopen.
  - `PublishSeatMap`: implement the ADR-029 family-scoped advisory-lock path, with organizer-scoped family resolution and re-resolution of the current version after taking the lock. Do not introduce a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the current-version row.
  - Preserve commit-before-event emission and all existing public-read invalidation behavior.

### Store call-site updates

Update organizer arguments in existing smoke tests and race tests:

- [`services/catalog/internal/store/archive_race_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/archive_race_smoke_test.go)
- [`services/catalog/internal/store/festival_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/festival_smoke_test.go)
- [`services/catalog/internal/store/season_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/season_smoke_test.go)
- [`services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_edit_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_edit_smoke_test.go)
- [`services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_publish_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_publish_smoke_test.go)

Add:

- `services/catalog/internal/store/organizer_predicate_smoke_test.go`
  - `//go:build smoke`
  - Real-PostgreSQL tests for all 13 operations.
  - Use the strongest forged position: attacker has the victim resource IDs and, where relevant, both victim row IDs.
  - Assert `ErrNotFound`, no victim mutation, and successful owner operation afterward.

### Back office

- [`web/backoffice/src/lib/catalog.ts`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/lib/catalog.ts:219)
  - Change `publishSeatMap(seatMapId, assertion)`.
  - Change `publishPerformance(performanceId, assertion)`.
  - Pass the assertion to `postCatalog`; remove comments claiming these writes intentionally omit it.

- [`web/backoffice/src/pages/venues/[id].astro`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/pages/venues/[id].astro:89)
  - Pass `staff.organizerAssertion` to `publishSeatMap`.

- [`web/backoffice/src/pages/events/new.astro`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/pages/events/new.astro:142)
  - Pass `staff.organizerAssertion` to `publishPerformance`.

- [`web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:243)
  - Update the publish-seat-map client test to supply `TEST_ASSERTION`.
  - Assert the organizer assertion header is sent.

### ADR

- [`docs/adr/ADR-058-catalog-organizer-assertion.md`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-058-catalog-organizer-assertion.md:195)
  - Amend, do not delete, item 5.
  - State that TKT-251 closes the path-id transition gap for a caller holding only the shared staff-write credential.
  - Retain the distinctions for compromised back office, signing-key holder, database writer, replay, roles, and multi-organizer staff.

## 3. Test plan

### COS 1 — verified organizer reaches every store operation

Tier: API contract plus handler wiring.

- Existing `TestEveryHandlerReadingTheVerifiedOrganizerRequiresTheAssertion` should discover all 13 new `organizerFor` calls and require matching OpenAPI security declarations.
- Existing AND-ness and unsafe-operation tests must pass automatically.
- Add a handler wiring test using a recording fake store to verify the organizer passed to every affected method equals the organizer in the verified assertion.

Mutations:

- Remove one operation’s `security:` block: AST-to-contract assertion must fail.
- Add assertion security to an operation whose handler does not call `organizerFor`: reverse-direction assertion must fail.
- Pass `uuid.Nil` or a request-derived value to one store call: the wiring test must fail.
- Split staff and assertion into separate security objects: the AND-ness test must fail.

### COS 2 — store-tier refusal for all 13 operations

Tier: real PostgreSQL smoke tests, because the authorization mechanism is the SQL predicate.

The new smoke test should cover:

- `AttachPerformanceToSeries`
- `AttachDayToFestival`
- `AttachSeriesToSeason`
- `AttachEventToSeason`
- `PublishSeries`
- `ArchiveSeries`
- `PublishFestival`
- `ArchiveFestival`
- `PublishPerformance`
- `ArchivePerformance`
- `CloseSlot`
- `ReopenSlot`
- `PublishSeatMap`

For each case:

1. Seed victim-owned resources.
2. Call the store using the attacker organizer and victim IDs.
3. Require `ErrNotFound`.
4. Re-read the victim row/membership/status and assert nothing changed.
5. Call with the victim organizer and assert the legitimate operation still succeeds.

Attach-specific fixtures must include:

- attacker holding both victim IDs, proving the old two-row organizer comparison cannot authorize the write;
- victim parent plus attacker-owned child;
- attacker-owned parent plus victim-owned child.

Mutations:

- Delete `AND organizer_id = $caller` from any locked lookup/update: the refusal test must go red.
- Restore an unscoped lookup and rely on `ErrOrganizerMismatch`: the test must go red because the required result is indistinguishable `ErrNotFound`.
- Remove the organizer predicate from `PublishPerformance`’s conditional update: the victim transition must occur and the test must fail.
- Remove the organizer predicate from the `ArchivePerformance`/closure `FOR UPDATE` lookup: the attacker must no longer get `ErrNotFound`, so the test fails.
- Replace the seat-map family advisory lock with a current-row `FOR UPDATE`: the concurrency/code-review check must reject the implementation; existing ADR-029 edit/pin race coverage must remain green.
- Run the same assertions against only the fake store as a negative control; deleting SQL predicates must not leave the real smoke tests green.

### COS 3 — ADR boundary is amended

Tier: documentation review, not an executable behavior test.

- Verify item 5 still exists.
- Verify it no longer says the 13 transitions remain open for the staff-token-holder adversary.
- Verify the database-writer limitation remains explicitly open.

Mutation:

- Delete item 5 or restore the obsolete “false of the transitions” claim; the ADR review checklist must reject the change.

## 4. Sequencing

1. Add the PostgreSQL smoke-test matrix and API wiring test first. They should fail against the current signatures/behavior.
2. Change `openapi.yaml` and all 13 handlers together. The AST invariant intentionally goes red if either side is staged independently.
3. Regenerate `openapi_gen.go` and TypeScript API outputs.
4. Change the `Store` interface and `Postgres` implementations.
5. Update the fake store and every existing direct store caller, including race tests.
6. Update the back-office client, two SSR callers, and its TypeScript API test.
7. Amend ADR-058 item 5.
8. Run focused catalog unit tests and smoke tests.
9. Regenerate once more if necessary, commit generated files, then run `make check`.
10. Do not edit tracked files while `make check` is running.

## 5. Risks

- The attach methods currently authorize by comparing two database rows. If both rows belong to the victim, an attacker can pass that comparison. Both row lookups need caller predicates.
- Returning `ErrOrganizerMismatch` leaks that a guessed ID exists. Cross-tenant misses must collapse to `ErrNotFound`.
- `PublishPerformance` currently performs an unscoped fallback read after a failed update. Adding the predicate only to the update is insufficient.
- Series and festival transitions must retain grouped-member rules: direct publication/archive of a grouped day remains refused.
- `PublishSeatMap` needs careful treatment of family locking and current-version resolution. The current implementation does not visibly implement the lock shape required by the brief.
- A fake-store API test can pass while SQL remains unscoped. The real smoke tests are mandatory.
- Existing smoke/race fixtures may need organizer IDs threaded through many calls; stale direct calls will cause compile failures.
- No browser test should be presented as proof of the upstream organizer header. The form markup is unchanged, and the SSR call is invisible to Playwright’s browser-side request observation.

## 6. Open decisions

1. **Exact publish-seat-map version semantics.**  
   Recommendation: preserve the current public idempotent behavior while adding family-lock serialization and organizer-scoped current-version resolution. If the endpoint must switch from the submitted version to the family’s newest version, update the OpenAPI description and add a focused smoke test before implementation.

2. **Shared SQL helper versus explicit predicates.**  
   Recommendation: use explicit organizer predicates in each entity-specific lookup. Reuse only the existing seat-map family-lock helper; broad generic helpers would obscure distinct transition and error semantics.

3. **Location of the residual sentinel test.**  
   The brief names `write_credential_test.go`, but the symbol currently lives in `channels_test.go`. Recommendation: keep the existing test in its actual file and extend or supplement it there rather than silently creating a duplicate with the same name.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan critique + finalization - by `main-agent` (config.models.planReview)

Adversarial pass over the `gpt-5.6-luna` draft. **Every file and symbol the draft names was verified
to exist at HEAD** (`transitionSeries`, `transitionFestival`, `toggleClosure`, `attachSeasonMember`,
`lockCurrentPublishedVersion`, `writeStoreError`, `fakeStore`, the 5 smoke-test call-site files, the
2 SSR callers, `web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:243`). No hallucinated seams.

**The kind=plan draft as amended below is the plan.**

#### Accepted as drafted

The core is right and I am not restating it: contract + handler + store move together (the AST
invariant forces it), organizer predicate inside the locked lookup, `ErrNotFound` on cross-tenant,
store-tier smoke tests as the only proof of the SQL, explicit per-entity predicates over a generic
helper (open decision 2 - accepted, and it is also the more reversible option), and the sequencing
that writes the failing tests first.

Two findings the drafter reached **independently** and which are the sharpest things in the plan:

- **`PublishPerformance`'s unscoped fallback read.** After a zero-row `UPDATE`, it re-reads via
  `getPerformance(ctx, id)` to classify *why* nothing flipped, returning `ErrGroupedSlotLifecycle` /
  `ErrNotSellable` / `ErrIllegalTransition`. Scoping only the `UPDATE` leaves that read unscoped, so
  a cross-tenant caller still learns the victim row's **status** through the error code. I found this
  in my own read; the drafter found it too. It is the least obvious defect in the ticket.
- **The attach trap generalizes.** The ticket named `AttachPerformanceToSeries`; the same two-row
  comparison is in `AttachDayToFestival` (`festivalOrg != performanceOrg`) and `attachSeasonMember`.

#### AMENDED - 1. The seat-map family lock does NOT apply to `PublishSeatMap` (my brief was wrong)

The draft's DoD item *"Seat-map publishing follows the family advisory-lock/re-resolve-current-
version rule from ADR-029"*, its Risk 6, and its open decision 1 are **rejected**. The drafter
flagged the mismatch honestly ("the current implementation does not visibly implement the lock
shape required by the brief") but resolved it toward the brief. The brief was wrong - I wrote it.

Evidence: `lockCurrentPublishedVersion` (postgres.go:1704) exists for operations that resolve *"the
family's current published version"* - `EditSeatMap` and `PinSeat` - because an edit INSERTs a new
version row, which never conflicts with a row lock on the old one. `PublishSeatMap` does not resolve
a current version: it flips **one specific draft row by id** (`UPDATE seat_maps SET status='published'
WHERE id=$1 AND status='draft'`), idempotently, pinned by `TestPublishSeatMapMonotonic`. Adopting the
family-lock shape would **change the endpoint's semantics** (which row gets published) to fix a race
it does not have.

**Amendment:** `PublishSeatMap` gets `AND organizer_id = $2` on its existing conditional `UPDATE`,
and the same predicate on the subsequent canonical re-read. No advisory lock, no version
re-resolution, no ADR-029 change. ADR-029 still governs `EditSeatMap`/`PinSeat`, untouched.
*Note `lockCurrentPublishedVersion` already takes `organizerID` and is already scoped* - the edit
path was never part of this gap.

#### AMENDED - 2. `transitionFestival` does not select `organizer_id` at all

The draft says "add organizer to the locked festival lookup". Precisely: `transitionFestival`
(postgres.go:1178) reads `SELECT status,shared_capacity FROM festivals WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE` - the
column is not in the projection. `transitionSeries` (postgres.go:1070) reads only `SELECT id`. So
this is *adding a predicate*, not *comparing an already-read value*: `... WHERE id=$1 AND
organizer_id=$2 FOR UPDATE`. Stated because "add organizer to the lookup" can be read as the
compare-after-read shape, which is exactly the trap this ticket exists to avoid.

#### AMENDED - 3. The sentinel test lives in `channels_test.go`, and EXTENDING it is required

The drafter caught that my brief mis-cited `write_credential_test.go`; verified - it is
`services/catalog/internal/api/channels_test.go:815`. Its open decision 3 recommends "extend or
supplement it there", which I accept, but I am **hardening it from optional to required**:
`TestStaffCredentialAloneCanNoLongerEnumerateOrMutateAcrossTenants` is today true of the 15 body
writes and **false of these 13**. Leaving it channels-only would let the ticket close while the
test that exists to detect this exact gap still passes for the wrong reason. It must gain a
transition case. ADR-058 says "if it ever fails, this ADR is wrong; do not delete it" - extending
its reach is the honest way to keep that true.

#### AMENDED - 4. The refusal must not leak through `writeStoreError` either

Not in the draft. `writeStoreError` (server.go:571) maps `ErrOrganizerMismatch` to **400 "entities
must belong to the same organizer"**, while `ErrNotFound` maps to 404. The store returning
`ErrNotFound` is necessary but not sufficient - the plan must assert the *HTTP* answer for a
cross-tenant transition is a 404 indistinguishable from an unknown id. `ErrOrganizerMismatch` stays
for the legitimate same-tenant case (attaching two of *your own* resources that belong to different
events), which is a real 400 and must not regress.

#### AMENDED - 5. No browser spec, and the reason is recorded rather than assumed

The draft's "no browser test" is correct and I am keeping it, with the justification stated so a
reviewer does not read it as a skipped gate: no form markup changes, and **a browser spec cannot see
the SSR handler's upstream call** - the page submits a form POST and the catalog call happens
server-side, so asserting the assertion header from Playwright would observe nothing (the vacuous
shape AGENTS.md records from TKT-244). The header is proven at the tier it exists:
`web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts` asserts `publishSeatMap` sends it. **`make browser` still gets
RUN** (the two SSR write paths are touched and must not 500 or lose their redirect); it just gains
no new spec. If `make browser` is red, that is a real failure, not a formality.

#### Decisions I took (autonomous mode, Gate 2)

Both open decisions the critique raised, resolved toward the most reversible option:

1. **Seat-map publish semantics** - resolved as *preserve current behavior, predicate only*
   (amendment 1). Strictly smaller than the alternative and changes no public semantics.
2. **Explicit predicates vs. a shared helper** - resolved as *explicit per entity* (drafter's own
   recommendation). Each transition has distinct error semantics; a generic helper would flatten them.
3. **Sentinel test placement** - resolved as *extend in `channels_test.go`*, no duplicate symbol.

Per the skill's required section - design elements **added** at 3b rather than accepted/amended from

1. **Amendment 4 in full** - the `writeStoreError` / HTTP-404-indistinguishability requirement and

3. **The `make browser` run/no-new-spec split** in amendment 5 - the drafter said "no browser test";
   the distinction between *running the gate* and *adding a spec* is mine.

These are named again here so the ai-review pass attacks them specifically.

#### TDD, tests observed red first

The store-tier test was written before the implementation and observed failing to compile against
the old signatures (`too many arguments in call to st.PublishPerformance`). After implementation it
passed, and then — the part that matters — **two mutants were run and killed**:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| Delete `AND organizer_id=$2` from `transitionSeries`' locked lookup | **RED** — `cross-tenant series publish = <nil>, want ErrNotFound` |
| Delete the scoped existence check in `PublishPerformance`'s zero-rows classification | **RED** — `cross-tenant publish = performance has no ticket type, want ErrNotFound` |

The second is the one worth reading: the mutant refused the *write* and still disclosed the victim
row's state through the error code. That is the defect the plan predicted and the test caught it.

#### A test I wrote, then rejected, then fixed

The sentinel-test extension (plan-final amendment 3) initially asserted only that a transition with
the credential alone returns 401. **It survived its mutation check**: removing the assertion
requirement from the contract left it green, because `organizerFor`'s fallback answers the same 401
and the two causes are indistinguishable from the status code. That is precisely the
green-test-that-cannot-reach-the-failing-state trap.

Rewritten to assert the **positive** case — with a valid assertion the request must get *past*
authentication and be answered by the handler (404 for an unknown id). Re-mutated: **RED**. The
AST-driven invariant also independently kills that mutant, so the boundary had real coverage either
way, but the test now proves what its name claims.

#### What changed vs. the approved plan

1. **An invariant the plan did not anticipate.** Once the 5 body-carrying transitions declared the
   assertion, `TestConvertedWriteSchemasRefuseASubmittedOrganizer` demanded they be
   `additionalProperties: false` — unsubmittable, not silently dropped (ADR-058 §1). None carried an
   `organizer_id` (nothing to delete), but a submitted one would have been ignored rather than
   refused. Five schemas closed. This is exactly the `governingTests` category: discoverable only by
   failing the gate.

2. **The gate found a real caller.** `make check` failed the first run on
   `TestCatalogPublicationAndStorefront` — `concurrent archive: status=401`. Not a regression: the
   boundary working. `postWithKey`/`postWithKeyAsync` in `smoke/` attached the staff credential to
   catalog URLs but no assertion, which was correct while the transitions took no organizer.
   `postJSON`/`postJSONAs` already sent both, which is why only the async/idempotency-key path
   failed. Fixed in the second commit.

3. **`getPerformance` was left alone.** The plan said to ensure the fallback read is scoped; it has
   5 callers, so rather than change its signature I added a scoped existence check at the one call
   site that needed it. Narrower and more reversible.

4. **`publishPerformance` had no back-office client test at all** — added one asserting both headers.

binding.rule: The field is DELETED, not validated. Catalog does not compare a submitted organizer against the verified one - there is nothing to submit. Every fix that *checks* a submitted value keeps the trust boundary in the client and merely moves where it leaks.

Both schemes are required TOGETHER, in one requirement object. One object means AND. Separate objects would mean OR - one bracket's difference - and the OR form means either credential alone suffices.

governingAdrs.why: The decision this ticket completes. s5 of 'what this does NOT close' states the boundary is FALSE for these 13 transitions and names the remedy shape: a store-tier organizer predicate, explicitly 'a different remedy from a credential'. That sentence becomes wrong the day this lands and must be AMENDED, not deleted (a COS).

Where a service auth guard lives. These 13 ARE contract operations, so their guard is a declared `security:` requirement enforced by the validator - not an inline check. ADR-058 applied this line as written; do not move it.

Catalog slot transition concurrency. State-deriving transitions decide UNDER A ROW LOCK and emit after commit. This is why the organizer predicate belongs INSIDE the locked lookup statement rather than in a check before it - a check outside the lock is a TOCTOU on the row the transition is about to move.

Name the adversary. This closes the staff-token holder, and does NOT close a writer with catalog DB access. State the claim for the adversary it actually holds against - two prior attempts at this exact claim in server.go were both wrong in good faith.

Seat identity pinning. publishSeatMap is one of the 13; seat-map edits are family-scoped under pg_advisory_xact_lock on map_family_id, NOT a row lock on the current version. Re-resolve the current version after taking the lock - a row lock on the old version never conflicts with an edit that INSERTs a new one.
Recorded the gap ADR-058 closes and the assumption it rested on. Useful precedent for how an honest residual is written down.

Partner credential identity - the per-organizer credential shape. ADR-058 s'Why not the alternatives' rejected it for staff tooling (tenant is a property of the signed-in human, not the process). Do not re-propose it here.

governingTests.rule: Derives its set from the Go AST - every method whose body mentions organizerFor - and asserts BOTH directions. A handler calling organizerFor without an operation-level assertion requirement FAILS, and a declared requirement whose handler does not read the scope also fails. The 13 enter coverage automatically; no new API-tier infrastructure needed.

The AND-ness. Both schemes must sit in ONE requirement object; the OR form passes securityRequires, passes a naive coverage test, and passes mutation testing. Write the block exactly as the 15 converted writes do.
Every unsafe operation is guarded and only those; safe operations must opt out with `security: []`. A new operation is closed by construction via the document-level default.

THE TEMPLATE for the 13 store-tier tests. Asserts at the tier the predicate lives, because a fake store scopes in Go and passes with the SQL deleted. Structure to copy: attacker holds the id AND the exact code (strongest forged position); refusal is ErrNotFound not a mismatch error (a distinguishing answer confirms a guessed id is real); nothing moved on the victim row; AND the owner is still unaffected - 'a boundary, not a wall'. Note the //go:build smoke tag: these run in the smoke stage, not test-go.

A handler reached with no verified scope refuses rather than writing for uuid.Nil. Exists because deleting the refusal left the whole package green - every other test drives the router, where the validator always fills the slot.
The inverted TKT-236 test. If it ever fails, ADR-058 is wrong - do not delete it. This ticket must EXTEND its reach to the transitions, since today it is true of the 15 writes and false of these 13.

reference.summary: CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN - one env scalar shared by one back office serving ALL staff. It names no tenant, which is exactly why a holder can reach any organizer's resources by id. Blast radius: every unsafe catalog write.

CATALOG_ORGANIZER_ASSERTION_KEY - catalog-only, never sent to the back office. A holder mints for any organizer, forever. Catalog refuses to start when it equals either credential: a key equal to the write credential would let anyone who can write mint their own tenancy.

Back-office seam: postCatalog(path, assertion, body) already takes the assertion; staff.organizerAssertion is already in scope in the handlers calling publishSeatMap / publishPerformance without it. No new plumbing.
